description.p: SuperV brings the Windows clipboard history to Linux. Press Super+V to see the last 25 things you copied, text and images, and click one to paste it into the app you are using.

ul.li: Text and image history, newest first
Click or press Enter to paste into the app you were using
Pin items so they survive restarts; everything else clears on reboot, like Windows
Choose your own shortcut, a System, Light or Dark theme, and the text size
Move and resize the panel; SuperV remembers both
Works on GNOME, Cinnamon, MATE and Xfce, on Wayland and X11 (KDE Plasma is experimental)

description.p: Private by default: SuperV never connects to the internet, keeps your history only on your computer, and skips copies marked as passwords. It is a single C program under 100 KB.

screenshot.caption: Your clipboard history: text, code, links and images, in dark or light
Pin, delete or clear items from the ⋯ menu

description.p: Screenshots in the app store: larger, landscape images that Ubuntu Software and GNOME Software can display.
Proper app-store listing: name, icon, screenshots, open-source licence, age rating and release notes in Ubuntu Software, GNOME Software and KDE Discover.
Packages for Fedora, openSUSE and Arch; SuperV restarts itself into a new version after an update; clicking outside always closes the panel; many fixes from a code review.
Browser image copies are saved as images; clearer settings menu with Reset; safer custom shortcuts.
